title: Dhan yoga: wealth combinations in your kundli, explained | Ask Tota
description: Dhan yoga links the lords of the 1st, 2nd, 5th, 9th and 11th houses. What counts, why most charts have one, and what makes a wealth yoga actually strong.
og_title: Dhan yoga, the wealth combinations, explained
og_description: Five houses, their lords, and the ways they connect. Why nearly every chart has some dhan yoga, and the strength tests that separate a real one.
h1: dhan yoga is about five houses talking to each other. here is how to tell if urs is loud
dek: vedic astrology reads wealth through a short list of houses: the 2nd for what u hold, the 11th for what comes in, the 5th and 9th for luck, the 1st for u. a dhan yoga is any meaningful connection between their lords, which is why almost everyone has one, and why strength is the whole story.

card_dek: the 1st, 2nd, 5th, 9th and 11th lords, and how they connect. why most charts have one, and the strength tests that matter.
llms_desc: how Vedic astrology reads wealth: the dhana houses (1st, 2nd, 5th, 9th, 11th), what forms a dhan yoga (conjunction, mutual aspect, exchange or placement between their lords), Jupiter and Venus as wealth significators, Lakshmi yoga, strength conditions, timing through dashas, and myths.

faq.a: a combination in a birth chart linking the lords of the wealth houses, mainly the 2nd and 11th, with the 1st, 5th and 9th. links can be by conjunction, mutual aspect, exchange of signs or one lord sitting in another's house.

faq.q: which houses show wealth in astrology?
faq.a: the 2nd house shows accumulated wealth and family resources. the 11th shows income and gains. the 5th and 9th, the trikonas, show merit and fortune. the 1st shows the self who earns and keeps it.

jupiter is the natural karaka of wealth and expansion, and of the 2nd and 11th houses. venus signifies luxury and comfort. mercury, trade and business. the lords of ur 2nd and 11th houses matter more personally than any single karaka.
very common in some form. with five houses' lords in play and four ways to connect, most charts have at least one link. what separates a significant dhan yoga is the strength of the planets involved.

faq.q: what makes a dhan yoga strong?
faq.a: the lords involved being dignified, placed in kendras or trikonas, free from combustion and heavy affliction, and connected to a strong lagna lord. weak or afflicted lords give a weaker yoga.
a classical wealth yoga where the 9th lord is strong and placed in a kendra or trikona in its own or exaltation sign, with a strong lagna lord. it is named after lakshmi, goddess of prosperity.

faq.q: when does dhan yoga give results?
faq.a: traditionally in the dashas and antardashas of the planets forming it, often triggered by jupiter's transits. a yoga describes potential; dashas are the timing.

it can be weakened when the planets involved are debilitated, combust, or sit in the 6th, 8th or 12th houses, or when the 2nd and 11th lords are heavily afflicted. weak does not mean poverty, just less support from that combination.

faq.q: does dhan yoga mean i will be rich?
faq.a: no. it is a traditional indicator of financial potential, not a guarantee. income depends on effort, opportunity, economy and choices. astrology should never be used for financial decisions.

faq.q: what is a 2nd and 11th lord exchange?
faq.a: a parivartana yoga where the 2nd lord sits in the 11th house and the 11th lord in the 2nd. it is one of the classic and strongest forms of dhan yoga.

faq.q: is dhan yoga the same as raj yoga?
faq.a: no. raj yoga links kendra and trikona lords and is about status and authority. dhan yoga links the wealth houses and is about resources. charts often have both, and they can overlap through the 1st, 5th and 9th.

the classical opposite: combinations, such as the 11th lord in a dusthana, that texts associate with financial struggle. like dhan yoga, it is a tendency to be weighed against the whole chart, not a sentence.
